Definition: a primary particle; properly, assigning a reason (used in argument, explanation or intensification; often with other particles):--and, as, because (that), but, even, for, indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, verily, what, why, yet.
BiblicalUsage: Gar is the little word for, the hinge on which an argument turns. Paul says in 1 Corinthians 10:1 that he would not have the brethren ignorant how all our fathers were under the cloud, and John says in 1 John 2:19 that they went out from us because they were not of us. The word gives the reason, and the reason carries the teaching.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the smallest words do the heaviest work in Scripture; for can turn a story into a doctrine, and I hold that the reasons God gives are always worth hearing.
